description: Full-history VRF selection scan (sim/find_selection.py, count=30 vault listings) over FWA acquisition logs. Each candidate is a real acquisition request whose real VRF word selects a vault listing when the vault posts 30 listings just before the request AND the acquisition queue is empty at the request AND no listing activates/reprices/leaves between the vault insertion and the selection (find_selection DISRUPT guard).
why_17_own_selections_unreachable: Each candidate requires the FWA acquisition queue EMPTY at the request so the vault inserted listings activate deterministically into known slots; with a non-empty queue FWA private staging FIFO reorders activation and the slot/weight the VRF word selects against cannot be reconstructed or controlled.

A journal accumulating 17 own selections needs 17 real acquisitions each selecting a distinct vault listing within ONE pinned fork pre-state, the vault holding all its listings active across the whole burst with no intervening sync and no disrupting listing event.

The 47 candidates over 251713 blocks are sparse and each is single-selection, queue-empty; the closest consecutive pair is 17 blocks apart with different purchasers and disrupting listing activity between them (that disruption is exactly why find_selection emits them as separate candidates). No 17-request burst meeting the exact-weight, queue-empty, no-disruption constraints exists in real history.
vm.createSelectFork re-forks and drops local state, so candidates at different blocks cannot be chained onto one fork; the suite is single-fork replay by design (AGENTS.md: never vm.transact).
